## CORRECTION to the comment above — the completed measurement REVERSES its verdict. This bug IS stale.

My previous comment stopped one query short and drew the wrong conclusion. Posting the correction
rather than editing it away, so the reasoning error stays on the record.

### What I got wrong

I reported 35 post-fix failures with `duration_s`>120 and `requests`=3 and called the bug live. What
I had not yet done was separate the failures by `output_tokens`. Once split, they are two disjoint
populations and only one of them is this bug's signature — and that one **stopped**.

### The decisive split (all 17 `/Users/joeoakhart/*/.rebar/usage.jsonl` logs, 1638 `overlap-judge` records, 2026-08-06T20:35Z -> 2026-08-12T01:29Z)

| population | n | `requests` | duration range | first | **last** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `output_tokens`=48000 (unbounded: 3 attempts x 16k cap) | 135 | 3 | 186.0-465.4s | 2026-08-06T23:36Z | **2026-08-10T17:39:48Z** |
| `output_tokens`=1024 (bounded by 7fa8102477) | 295 | **1, always** | **1.5-29.8s** | 2026-08-09T17:26Z | 2026-08-12T01:29Z |

* Bounded-path failures above 120s: **zero**.
* Bounded-path failures in this bug's 312-381s band: **zero**.
* The 48000-token population has produced **nothing since 2026-08-10T17:39:48Z**.

Post-checkout-update traffic is unambiguous — 149 `overlap-judge` calls after 2026-08-11T18:07Z,
67 of them failures, **every one bounded** (`output_tokens`=1024, `requests`=1), max duration across
all 149 calls **24.0s**. The 312-381s / `requests`=3 band is now structurally unreachable: with
`transport_attempt_limit=1` and `request_timeout_limit_s=60` a single request cannot spend 300s.

### So the triage hypothesis was right

`7fa8102477` ("Bound malformed overlap judge calls", 2026-08-08 23:25 -0700, ticket
[rebar:22da-e9a6-63e7-49e5]) killed this failure mode. The 2026-08-09/08-10 occurrences I cited as
counter-evidence were **stale checkouts and long-lived processes still executing pre-fix code**, not
current-build failures. That is independently confirmed by [rebar:3939-d68c-6e99-498d], whose own
investigation landed on the identical cutoff — "every 48000-token failure is timestamped at or
before 2026-08-10T17:39" — reached from different data than mine. Two independent measurements
converging on the same timestamp is about as good as this evidence gets.

Related: [rebar:b273-e0ba-f719-4f1c] tracks the actual remaining hazard — a gate run does not warn
when its running build is behind the base ref, which is precisely what made these stale-build
failures look live in the telemetry. That ticket stays open; it is the real lesson here.

### The `judge_one` lead is also closed out

My previous comment flagged that `7fa8102477` bounded only `judge_batch` (judge.py:171-185) and left
`judge_one` (judge.py:133-141) unbounded. That is textually true but not load-bearing:
`judge_one` has **no production caller** — `wire.py -> judge() -> judge_batch` at judge.py:284-285 is
the only live path, and the module's in-code "volume site" comment on `judge_one` is stale.
[rebar:3939-d68c-6e99-498d] filed exactly this and closed it `not_a_bug` for the same reason.

### Answers to the acceptance criteria, from measurement

The ACs asked for the mechanism, and the measurement does establish it, so recording it before close:

1. **Mechanism (AC1/AC2): output-retry exhaustion, not a provider-side timeout and not retry of a
   transport error.** Every long failure carries `finish_reason=length` and exactly 48000 output
   tokens = 3 attempts (pydantic-ai `OUTPUT_RETRIES=2` default) x the 16000-token default cap. The
   model ran to the output ceiling, the structured parse failed, it retried, three times, ~310s.
   Successful calls on the same path show 16091 / 16036 / 16323 / 16102 / 32035 output tokens,
   confirming the 16k-per-request ceiling. `model=bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` throughout,
   so this is neither the [rebar:2876-7958-8dee-4882] direct-Anthropic 401 misroute (0.2s) nor the
   [rebar:895c-3eb2-043a-4de1] pre-response 400 (`requests`=0).
2. **Effect on the verdict (AC3):** `judge_one` and `judge_batch` both swallow any exception and
   return `_ABSTAIN`, so an overlap-judge failure never fails a review — it silently disables
   cross-reviewer dedup for the affected pairs and duplicate findings survive into the verdict with
   no signal that dedup did not run. On the batch path the whole batch abstains together. This is
   unchanged by the fix; the fix changed its cost (~$132 of measured waste -> ~$0.02 per failure),
   not its semantics.
3. **Regression test (AC4): void with the premise.** `7fa8102477` landed its own bounds coverage
   (`tests/unit/test_overlap_judge.py` +141 lines, `tests/unit/test_runner_hardening.py`,
   `tests/unit/test_settings_builders_seam.py`). A regression test for this ticket would test the
   same seam that fix already pins.

### Closing

Closing as **duplicate** of [rebar:22da-e9a6-63e7-49e5], the ticket whose fix eliminated this
failure mode. Nothing here is actionable that is not already carried by
[rebar:b273-e0ba-f719-4f1c] (stale-build blindness).

Residual, non-blocking, inherited from 3939: a batch whose legitimate verdict exceeds 1024 output
tokens now abstains — an overlap-recall loss worth revisiting only if drain-abstain rates grow.

All evidence gathered read-only; no repository or store state changed.
